identity.description: Multivariate linear dynamics over K aligned series: each series is regressed on p lags of ALL series, capturing cross-series lead-lag interdependence (Granger structure, impulse responses). The observed K-vector IS the state; the lag-coefficient matrices are its linear transition law — the fully-observed continuous analog of this family, as the Markov chain is its discrete one.

consumes.note: K ALIGNED series sharing one regular time index, carried as a wide numeric frame — the interim convention for a multivariate bundle on the singular `series` port
consumes.portTypeProposal: `series` reads as singular; VAR's true input is an aligned K-variate bundle. Propose for U2 either a `series:multi` (or `panel`) port type, or an explicit arity-K binding rule on `series`. Until decided, the wide-frame-on-`series` convention above is declared here rather than silently assumed.

emits.note: joint multivariate forecast — one forecast-series per input column, intervals from the fitted innovation covariance
the p lag-coefficient matrices + innovation covariance — the Granger/IRF structure; the 'who leads whom' story

maxlags.note: lag order p — selected by information criterion; parameters grow as K^2 per added lag

ic.note: criterion for automatic lag selection within maxlags — the family's model-selection lens applied to lag depth

invariances.why: per-equation OLS is equivariant under per-series rescaling — coefficients and forecasts rescale accordingly; the fitted dynamics are isomorphic
linearity holds in one parameterization; log-transforming a series changes the joint dynamics being estimated
OLS on lagged design matrices needs a complete, aligned, gap-free panel — a NaN in any series knocks out whole rows across all equations
assumes joint weak STATIONARITY of the K-vector and Gaussian innovations for valid intervals; nonstationary inputs produce spurious dynamics
K^2·p + K parameters against T time points — the parameter count is quadratic in the number of series, so modest K at short T overfits fast
forecasting is iterated application of the fitted linear dynamics — principled while the system is stable (all companion eigenvalues inside the unit circle)

featureStats.why: (K^2·p + K) against series length T is the overparameterization ratio — the quadratic-in-K parameter count is THIS model's failure axis and the gate to fewer series or lags
off-diagonal lead-lag correlation is the evidence cross-series dynamics exist; if the structure is diagonal, K univariate ARIMAs match the VAR without the K^2 cost
each series must be (difference-)stationary before joint OLS — regressing nonstationary series on each other manufactures spurious relationships

modelMetrics.why: likelihood rises with every added lag while parameters grow by K^2 — the information-criterion curve is the honest lag-depth selector
the joint model must beat the K-univariate-ARIMA floor out of sample, or the cross-series machinery is not earning its parameters
the largest companion-matrix eigenvalue is the stability certificate — modulus >= 1 means the fitted system is explosive and its forecasts diverge

edgeCases.note: difference first, or the VECM sibling for cointegrated systems

edgeCases.condition: T too small for K^2·p parameters
misaligned or gapped time indexes across series
edgeCases.behavior: silent row loss or invalid alignment

edgeCases.condition: one series a near-linear combination of others

driver.wrapperNeeds: multi-series adapter: (time_col, [value_cols...]) -> wide aligned frame; forecast returns a K-column frame — one forecast-series per input column; must NOT assume a single value_col (the portTypeProposal nuance made operational)
driver.threadSafety: per-equation OLS; fit is single-threaded and deterministic

placementClaims.why: a NaN anywhere in the panel drops that time row from every equation; gaps need time-aware interpolation before the lagged design is built
log (and differencing to stationarity) linearizes multiplicative growth and protects against spurious regression — the stationarity prerequisite made concrete
per-series rescaling is absorbed equivariantly by the coefficients; standardization changes nothing about fit or forecasts
numeric series only — nothing categorical reaches the design matrix
